subject: n_eff variation & step-size adjusted U-turn condition

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: n_eff variation & step-size adjusted U-turn condition
parts:
I used Daniel's spiffy new testing code to run
all the BUGS models with n_eff and timing with
the current unadjusted U-turn condition and the
one adjusted for step sizes.

The frightening part of the results is that just
measuring the parameters with the minimum n_eff,
you see variation of a factor of 10 from run to
run of the same sampler. You also see variations
like that between the samplers.

The mean and median n_eff are more stable.

This has serious implications for how we're going to
measure and report timings. I'm not sure what it
means for measuring convergence. Sometimes the param
with the min n_eff has an n_eff of 2 or 5 when the
max has an n_eff of 2000. Clearly the params aren't
mixing equally well.

I'll need to run more tests to get a sense of
the trends and variations.

I've attached three runs of the output in .csv format.
The new is the adjusted one, and I ran once in clang++
and once in g++.

- Bob
